Hi all! I'm Antoine (GitHub: AntoineduFresne). I'd like to start contributing to Mathlib: I already contribute to Cslib. I have a sorry-free formalization of Dilworth's theorem and its dual, Mirsky's theorem, for finite partial orders (via Galvin's induction; and there is no dependency on König's theorem).

I know Vlad Tsyrklevich has a version in a personal repo and has upstreamed some supporting IsChain/IsAntichain lemmas; since the theorems themselves aren't in Mathlib yet, I went ahead and formalized them. My proof is self-contained and takes a different, Finset-based route (weak + strong duality, no min'/max' over families of sets, which I think is better suited as an API: happy to discuss about this), so it doesn't build on his material: though I'd genuinely like to hear what people think of the approach before committing to it.

Could I be added to the leanprover-community organisation so I can push a branch, or should I just fork mathlib4 and open a standard PR? Thanks!
Hi Antoine, these days the mechanism to contribute is through GitHub forks.

Update: I split a small lemma out of #40741 into its own PR: #42590. It adds IsMaxAntichain.upperClosure_union_lowerClosure to Mathlib/Order/UpperLower/Closure.lean, and it is about ten lines.

How can I add the easy label to it?

You can add easy by commenting easy but I think this is actually not a good use of the tag. easy is generally for obvious very simple corrections, i.e. typos or trivial generalizations. Anything where someone might have feedback or require looking at the surrounding API is probably not a good candidate
Ok thank you for the information, then lets not put easy.
